tagline: Out from a green that once took frogs for an army.
intro: Route 203 leaves Route 32 in South Windham, crosses the Shetucket River and runs north about a mile and a half to the green at Windham Center. From there Route 14 heads east as Scotland Road, four mostly rural miles over to Scotland.

Windham Center became the county seat in 1726 and did well on the courthouse trade. On a summer night in 1754 its people woke to a din they took for an enemy attack, and an armed scouting party went out to meet it. Over the hill at Follett's Pond they found bullfrogs. The town adopted the frog.

moments.title: Windham Center
moments.text: On the green, with the Congregational church, stands the 1832 Windham Bank, which once put frogs on its currency and has been the free library since 1896.

moments.title: Samuel Huntington Birthplace
moments.text: A saltbox from the early 1700s, its woodwork and plaster almost all original, where the signer of the Declaration and later governor was born in 1731.

moments.title: Scotland
moments.text: Isaac Magoon bought the land from Windham in 1700 and named it for his ancestral home, and a tool museum in the library building now keeps more than 1,200 antique woodworking planes.
